thread:
Avery: quick heads up — noticed a tenant complaining that some v2-targeted requests are being billed against their v1 quota. not widespread but reproducible in the staging shard
Maria: ugh, that sounds like a routing/tagging mismatch. do you have examples?
Avery: yep. sample req captured: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \
  -H 'X-Client-Version: v2' \
  -H 'X-Session-Id: sess-123' \
  -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
But our billing rows show the token usage under the tenant's v1 bucket for the same time window.
Sahil: is the session affinity key maybe still pointing at an older route instance that tags as v1? we persist route metadata per session for 24h, right? :thinking_face: 
Jordan: we do sticky by session id but we also have a fallback that rewrites the route header when a model variant isn't available. could be a path where the header rewrite happens after the billing attribution event.
Maria: good call. billing attribution is keyed off the routing snapshot at start-of-request. if any middleware rewrites after that, billing won't see it.
Avery: that would explain it — the router decided to funnel to a compatible variant (v1) during a brief capacity pressure. the request header in the backend shows v2 -> routed to compat-v1, and billing logged compat-v1.
Sahil: then this is behavior: routing fallbacks can change the effective model, which affects quota. Are we okay with that semantically? tenants likely expect header X-Client-Version to map to billed version.
Jordan: historically we've treated routing decision as authoritative for billing, not the original client header. changing that now is risky. we already have tenants on reserved capacity who rely on routing to enforce committed capacity.
Maria: proposal: add an attribute to routing decisions called "billing_version" that is explicitly set when a fallback path is taken. Billing would prefer billing_version if present, else derived version. That makes it explicit.
Avery: sounds reasonable. also need console UX — show on the request trace which version was billed and why. right now traces only show final model id, not the billing tag.
Sahil: small opt-in toggle in Console: "Bill by client-declared version (best-effort)" — default off. if on, we attempt to bill to the header version even if routed elsewhere, but add a warning and a potential overcommit note.
Jordan: ⛔️ that would risk double-counting reserved capacity. customers with dedicated pools would be angry if we billed to their v2 quota while actually running on v1 infra.
Maria: maybe split behavior per deployment mode: Hosted API = billing follows routing (current), Dedicated = billing follows pin (tenant config) unless tenant explicitly opts into best-effort header billing.
Avery: implementation note: attribution happens in the ingress layer before full routing resolution. If we want billing_version to reflect post-fallback state, we need to materialize routing fallback outcome back to the ingress sync path or emit a deferred billing event once model selection completes.
Sahil: deferred billing event seems safer: ingress emits a placeholder, runtime emits finalBillingTag when selection completes, billing reconciler updates rows. might add ~50ms to billing latency but accuracy up.
Jordan: can we avoid schema churn? add final_billing_tag as optional field in the request-span proto. reconciler will do upsert semantics.
Maria: yep. update traces, console, and add a telemetry stat for "billing_tag_mismatch" when initial tag != final tag. Send an alert if >0.1% of requests for a tenant.
Avery: I'll open a tiny RFC and include example proto diff + reconciler flow. PR will propose: 
- add optional final_billing_tag to request span
- ingress emits initial tag (client header or default)
- runtime emits final tag after fallback resolution
- billing reconciler upserts final tag when present
- console shows billed tag and a short reason string (fallback|pinned|capacity|manual)

Jordan: agree. also add a safety: if final tag indicates a tenant reserved pool and the ingress initial tag was a different tenant, block auto-billing change (prevent cross-tenant misbilling).
Sahil: +1. and add unit tests for the reconciler race (ingress placeholder -> runtime final emits concurrently).
Maria: UX: console trace can show a diff view like: "requested: v2 -> routed: compat-v1 (billing: compat-v1)" with a tooltip linking to routing decision logs.
Avery: thanks — I'll draft RFC and prototype reconciler hook. tagging folks for review: @Maria @Sahil @Jordan. deploy-bot: creating a ticket in infra backlog.
deploy-bot: Created INFRA-2249: routing -> billing tag reconciliation (see https://tickets.redwood.ai/INFRA-2249)
Jordan: neat. can we also add an alert for tenants that see steady-state >1% mismatch? that's a sign of routing pressure or misconfigured pins.
Maria: will add to telemetry playbook. thanks all.
Sahil: thanks — good catch, Avery :thumbsup:
Avery: will follow up with RFC link shortly.
